note: Upstream Python package at the tag. The compiled extensions (csrc) come from the pinned container's install of the same tag; tools/stage-vllm-overlay.sh layers this tree over that install. vllm/vllm/config/fault_tolerance.py is stored LF-normalized (upstream has CRLF).

local_patches.why: back the CUDA caching allocator with expandable (VMM) segments, set before CUDA is initialized and again in Worker.init_device; only the mapping under an allocator segment changes (VLLM_EXPANDABLE_SEGMENTS=0 keeps the default allocator)
GB10 exposes no NVML memory clock; fall back to 273 GB/s for humming's tuning heuristic
VLLM_HUMMING_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 turns on humming's deterministic MoE kernels without the global batch-invariant mode (which forces CUTLASS W4A4 on W4A16 linears)

when the optional l2pf kernel package (harness/kernels/l2pf) is importable, the FULL CUDA graph gets one extra side-stream node per GEMM that L2-prefetches the first tiles of the next GEMM's weights; the GEMM sites are recorded on the warm-up run before the capture, only model parameters are prefetched, and no kernel on the main stream changes (L2PF=0 turns it off)

the accepted glimmer_fp8_ext G2 tile serves the supported small FP8 GEMMs on GB10 with the stock accumulation order and scale rounding. L2 prefetch records the actual native launch or the stock CUTLASS overload with the same model weight pointer

local_patches.file: vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/ssd_pinned_configs.py (+ pins in ssd_state_passing.py, ssd_bmm.py, ssd_chunk_scan.py, ssd_chunk_state.py)
local_patches.why: Triton autotune picked different SSD tile configs per boot on GB10, making the same prompt yield one of two token streams; each kernel is pinned to one config (VLLM_MAMBA_SSD_AUTOTUNE=1 restores autotuning)

the attention output gate projection reads the layer input, so for decode-sized batches it is launched before attention and the attention chain (QK-norm, RoPE, KV-cache write, attention) runs beside it on a high-priority side stream; fork, switch and join are graph splitting points, so the gate projection is a compiled piece of its own and the FULL CUDA graph gets a fork and a join; the same kernels run on the same inputs, unquantized (cuBLAS) gate projections keep the stock order (VLLM_MUSE_GLIMMER_GATE_STREAM=0 turns it off)
skip the MTP drafter when every request in the batch has max_tokens == 1: its drafts are never verified, and the drafter's pass over the prompt delayed the sampled token (the timed prefill)

NVFP4 W4A16 weights much larger than L2 (MLP gate_up and down) run calls of 128 rows or more through harness/kernels/marlinw when it is built (the Marlin kernel body on the same work slices as ops.marlin_gemm, handed out column-major); a layer without it runs prompt-sized calls as ops.marlin_gemm on column slices of a slice-major copy of the same prepared weight where both schedules compute every tile whole-K with the same config, else the single call; each path is admitted per layer by a load-time bitwise comparison with the single call

in-process engine core for the single-request engine loop: InprocClient pauses automatic garbage collection while the engine has work and drains a finished request's queued batch on abort (no busy loop does it in this mode); hostfast.py also restricts the process to the highest-capacity CPU cores when the cores differ, failing soft (VLLM_HOSTFAST_GC=0 and VLLM_HOSTFAST_PIN=0 switch each off)

one-token FP8 w8a8 GEMMs (decode) run through musefp8, a hand-written mma.sync m16n8k32 e4m3 GEMV that issues the same instruction chain in the same k order as cutlass_scaled_mm's SM120 M16 kernel and the same ScaledEpilogue (bf16_rn(scale_a * fp32(scale_b * acc))), reading a fragment-ordered copy of each weight (registered as a layer buffer) with L2 evict-first loads; every layer is admitted only after a load-time bitwise comparison with cutlass_scaled_mm; other row counts keep glimmer_fp8 / cutlass; the op is an l2pf site (MUSEFP8=0 disables, MUSEFP8_L2PF=0 drops it from the prefetch chain). When harness/kernels/muserans is built, each FP8 weight is instead stored as an exponent-pair rANS stream with raw sign|mantissa nibbles (lossless, ~0.84 of the bytes on this checkpoint) and decoded inside the same GEMV right before the same mma.sync chain, so the output bits are unchanged and the decode step reads fewer bytes; admitted per layer by the same bitwise check (MUSERANS=0 keeps the uncompressed copy) Imported from zereraz's Yukon submission cdefbb34-137b-48d9-9179-db4b540fbf57 (evaluation source 56791c43d807320c42d93b023678800489f6500c).

Uses zereraz's published 6-bit palette implementation from cdefbb34 / 56791c43 for one-row NVFP4 decode after the per-layer bitwise admission check. The existing BF16 and FP8 SwiGLU prefill and narrow down operation signatures preserve their arguments.

The single-device 512-row static FP8 MLP gate/up dispatches to harness/kernels/muse_fp8_swiglu when its down projection accepts static FP8. Alternating checkpoint output columns brings the BF16 gate and up values into one CUTLASS thread fragment. The arithmetic uses the G2 scaled-MM multiply order and the existing BF16 SiLU lookup before packing the down-scale E4M3 byte. The input uses its original FP8 quantizer before shape dispatch.

Carries only ArthurOstapenko's prompt query normalization and RoPE launcher and installation hook from Yukon submission fa040f4a-ca7e-42dd-8f50-8f1aadfc8d9b (ranked aa3a2e54b58675aa76f633bd31a3d07b0e4d41ab), first published in e7600084-0e57-465b-8c3c-1df33c51dd94. Before replacing a matching compiled kernel, the launcher compares output bits against the actual stock compiler kernel. The default minimum batch size is 128 tokens.

The unquantized BF16 Muse Glimmer QKV and output gate on one CUDA device admit the one-row lane-striped GEMV only after a complete lossless weight check and per-layer bitwise cuBLAS comparisons. It keeps the original lane accumulation and warp fold. Larger row counts, bias and other weights retain the stock linear method. The original weights remain the fallback and the L2 site reads only the registered compact buffer. MUSE_BF16_LANE=0 selects the original paths.

Keep the full compiled backbone and specialize only the final two independent-row NVFP4 projection launches inside the logits-only prefill capture. Retain both operator output shapes and the ordered K partition for the sampled tile. Full-output consumers use the original projection launches.

the paired gate/up SwiGLU kernel at 512 rows (harness/kernels/marlinw/csrc/marlinw_swiglu.cu, the mechanism of Yukon entry 95faadcd) is used for a gate_up layer only after a load-time bitwise comparison of its output with the single ops.marlin_gemm call followed by the compiled SiLU-and-mul body (fp32 silu(g) = g / (exp(-g) + 1) times up, one bf16 rounding) on three input families; a layer that differs keeps the projection and the compiled glue

from Yukon entry 95faadcd (its narrow routes derive from entry e786622e), carried in entry 67957adf: at 512 rows the NVFP4 gate_up (39936 x 6656) runs a whole-K 64x128 Marlin tile that halves each stock 256-column tile, the NVFP4 down (6656 x 19968) runs a 64x128 tile whose work list keeps every stock K range, split index and fold order with both halves of a stock tile in one block, each admitted per layer by a load-time bitwise comparison with the single ops.marlin_gemm call; where down_proj is an NVFP4 Marlin layer (bf16 input) the compiled model calls a paired kernel that computes 64 gate and 64 up columns of one CTA over the whole K, rounds each to bf16 as the projection does, and applies silu(gate) * up with the compiled SiLU-and-mul arithmetic (a table of the fp32 silu of every bf16 gate value, fp32 multiply, one bf16 rounding)

from Yukon entry 95faadcd (extending the G2 tile of entry 4adc6cad), carried in entry 67957adf: FP8 w8a8 calls of a few rows on the listed checkpoint shapes run the same CUTLASS SM120 pingpong GEMM with a 16x32x512 tile; every output element keeps the ascending sequence of k32 MMA fragments into one fp32 accumulator and the same epilogue, with no split-K

whole-forward CUDA graph for one fresh, unpadded, single-request 512-token prefill, captured at boot in its own pool after two eager forwards; a step replays it only when every host scalar of its attention metadata and model inputs equals the captured one, else it runs eager; logits stay outside the graph; the warm-up adds one 512-token seed round; VLLM_PREFILL_GRAPH=0 switches it off (as in Yukon entries 95faadcd and 67957adf; port of entry c1e4b913 via entries ff28cfe8 and b3073f3d)

from Yukon entry 67957adf: at 512 rows, where an NVFP4 gate_up is followed by an FP8 down_proj with a per-tensor static input scale (layers 1-4 and 12 of this checkpoint), the paired gate/up kernel computes silu(gate) * up in fp32 from the bf16-rounded projections, multiplies by 1 / scale, clamps to +-448 and stores e4m3, the arithmetic of the compiled SiLU-and-mul plus FP8 quantization (no bf16 rounding of the product); the down projection takes that activation as a QuantizedActivation and skips its own quantization. Each MLP is admitted only after a load-time comparison, byte for byte, of the fused output with the single ops.marlin_gemm call followed by a Triton copy of the compiled SiLU-and-mul FP8 quantization body, with the down projection's own scale, on four input families; an MLP that differs keeps the projection and the compiled glue

full decode checks of the lossless decode layouts of Yukon entries cdefbb34 (zereraz) and 67957adf (kaankolcu): an FP8 weight stored as an exponent-pair rANS stream (the 4-bit exponents of two adjacent weights form one symbol of a static 12-bit-probability table per tensor, interleaved 32-bit rANS states; sign and mantissa kept raw as a nibble plane) is decoded in full with rans_unpack, and the fragment-ordered uncompressed copy is put back in row order, and either must equal every byte of the loaded weight before the GEMV check runs; the NVFP4 group-16 block scales stored as 6-bit codes into a 64-entry per-layer palette are expanded in full and must equal the loaded Marlin scales byte for byte (the tile-major weight copy likewise), and the one-row GEMV must then equal ops.marlin_gemm itself on three inputs; boot lines count the layers and bytes compared; a layer that fails keeps the uncompressed path

GEMMs whose weights exceed L2PF_MAX_WEIGHT_MB (the MLP) get a weight-head prefetch sized to the window ahead of them: L2PF_MB_MLP_NORM (2.25 MiB) ahead of a GEMM that follows a norm (gate_up), L2PF_MB_MLP_ACT (0.5 MiB) ahead of one that follows the previous large GEMM's activation (down); only the prefetch side branch changes (same main-stream kernels, arguments and order), every range is still checked to lie inside a model tensor; L2PF_MLP=0 restores the skip

local_patches.file: harness/kernels/muse_fp8_swiglu, harness/kernels/sandwich, harness/kernels/decode6, harness/kernels/muse_bf16_lane, harness/kernels/muse_final_slab; vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py, vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/glimmer_fp8.py, vllm/model_executor/models/muse_glimmer.py, vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py, vllm/v1/worker/gpu/prefill_graph.py, harness/vllm_resident/backends.py
local_patches.why: from Yukon entries 1c021643 and 74c0e315 (kaankolcu), carried as published: the 512-row FP8 gate/up GEMM with SiLU-and-mul and the down projection's FP8 quantization in its epilogue, the native post-down residual normalization kernel, the independent gate/up decode tiles of the 6-bit scale GEMV, the lane-packed one-row BF16 attention GEMV and the final-row prefill tile; the entries above describe each mechanism. The four-state rANS stream of the FP8 down projection that 1c021643 adds is not carried: harness/kernels/muserans is the two-state stream and GEMV of the accepted record, as in Yukon entry ea49bd77 (e-man07)

load-time checks for the mechanisms of entries 1c021643 and 74c0e315: the column-paired FP8 gate/up copy is kept only if its 512-row e4m3 output equals the layer's FP8 GEMM (glimmer::fp8_scaled_mm) followed by the compiled SiLU-and-mul FP8 quantization body with the down projection's own input scale on five input families; the independent gate/up decode tiles are compared with ops.marlin_gemm at one row on the three full-check inputs; a matched compiled sandwich kernel object is admitted per row count at its first launch outside graph capture after the compiled and the native kernel give equal bytes in every buffer on copies of the real arguments and on two generated inputs; the final-row prefill tile is prepared only if its gate/up and down launches equal the last 64 rows of the full 512-row launches on three inputs; whatever differs keeps the original path, and boot and first-call lines count each

a wrapped GEMM entry point that is re-entered through itself (a Python dispatch path that looks the overload up by name finds the wrapper) is recorded once, at the outermost call: the one-row BF16 lane GEMV of entry 74c0e315 was recorded as two prefetch sites (272 sites instead of 260); prefetch descriptors only, no kernel or argument changes
